T.data_reference: lynch2015bioenergetic; operating point 20 C, the temperature Lynch & Marinov normalise maintenance costs to

R.data_reference: definitional; gas constant, as the library's SN modules

C_glc_init.data_reference: unreferenced_placeholder; design value; no measurement found (searched 2026-10-23): free glucose inside the cell (no E. coli measurement: PTS uptake delivers G6P). glucose inside an uptake-limited cell at rest: low, so glycolysis has ~50x headroom (growing fermenters run 10-40x their maintenance flux)

C_lac_init.data_reference: calibrated: steady state of the lumped cell (export by the membrane carrier = production)

C_G6P_init.data_reference: chassagnole2002dynamic; glucose 6-phosphate in the resting cell, a chosen operating point in the measured range: E. coli in glucose-limited chemostat culture (D = 0.1 /h) 3.48 mM G6P (Chassagnole et al. 2002, Table V; the initial value of their model, BioModels BIOMD0000000051), exponentially growing on glucose 8.8 mM hexose phosphates (G6P + F6P + G1P; Bennett et al. 2009, Table 1, which does not resolve G6P). 1 mM, below the growing cells' values, as the level-1 cell runs at its maintenance flux (confidence: medium; the range 0.5-4 mM is well supported, the exact resting value is a choice)

C_ATP_init.data_reference: bennett2009absolute; glucose-fed, exponentially growing E. coli: ATP 9.6 mM

C_ADP_init.data_reference: bennett2009absolute; glucose-fed, exponentially growing E. coli: ADP 0.56 mM (Table 1)

C_Pi_init.data_reference: amin1995dual; cytoplasmic Pi of E. coli near 10 mM in typical growth (BioNumbers BNID 105540, from Amin & Peterkofsky 1995 and Rao & Torriani 1994); 20-30 mM in carbon-starved cells

V_c.data_reference: geometry: disc of radius 1 um, 2 um deep (the starting cell)

T_ref.data_reference: lynch2015bioenergetic; operating point 20 C, the temperature Lynch & Marinov normalise maintenance costs to

dT_Q10.data_reference: definitional; definition of Q10 (rate ratio per 10 K)

c_std.data_reference: definitional; standard concentration 1 M for thermodynamic factors

dG0_ferm.data_reference: beber2022equilibrator; glucose -> 2 lactate: -193.3 +- 3.7 kJ/mol (the same for D- and L-lactate), eQuilibrator 3.0 at pH 7.0, pMg 3, I 0.25 M, 25 C (under 0.5 kJ/mol from its value at 20 C); the four standard Gibbs energies are one set

dG0_hyd.data_reference: beber2022equilibrator; ATP + H2O -> ADP + Pi: -27.4 +- 0.6 kJ/mol, eQuilibrator 3.0 at pH 7.0, pMg 3, I 0.25 M, 25 C (under 0.5 kJ/mol from its value at 20 C); the four standard Gibbs energies are one set

V_gly.data_reference: calibrated: glycolysis supplies the total ATP turnover (lynch2015bioenergetic maintenance at 20 C) at the default steady state

K_glc.data_reference: miller2004identifying; lumped glycolysis affinity for glucose: E. coli glucokinase Km 0.076 mM (Miller 2004), 0.15 mM (arora1995glucokinase), 0.78 mM (meyer1997molecular). Wild-type E. coli takes glucose up mostly through the PTS

K_ATP_hk.data_reference: miller2004identifying; ATP for half-rate of the hexokinase step: E. coli glucokinase Km(ATP) 0.26 mM (pH 7.6, 25 C; 0.5 and 3.76 mM in arora1995glucokinase and meyer1997molecular). Far below the cell's 9.6 mM, so it acts only as ATP runs out

dG0_hk.data_reference: beber2022equilibrator; glucose + ATP -> glucose 6-phosphate + ADP: -17.9 +- 0.8 kJ/mol, eQuilibrator 3.0 at pH 7.0, pMg 3, I 0.25 M, 25 C (under 0.5 kJ/mol from its value at 20 C); the four standard Gibbs energies are one set

h_hk.data_reference: alberty1998calculation; heat released by glucose + ATP -> glucose 6-phosphate + ADP: 21.58 kJ/mol from Alberty's species enthalpies (25 C, I = 0; no buffer heat, as h_ATP); calorimetry of yeast hexokinase PI gives 21.3 (bianconi2003calorimetric)

V_lg.data_reference: derived: lower_glycolysis_headroom x resting glycolytic flux / its ADP and Pi saturation at rest (lower_glycolysis_headroom: unreferenced_placeholder, placeholder; maintenance_coefficient: lynch2015bioenergetic, sourced; K_ADP_gly: chassagnole2002dynamic, sourced; K_Pi_gly: eyschen1999engineered, sourced)

K_G6P_lg.data_reference: derived: steady state of the lower glycolysis at rest: G6P_i (headroom - 1)^(1/n_G6P_lg) (G6P_i: chassagnole2002dynamic, design; lower_glycolysis_headroom: unreferenced_placeholder, placeholder; n_G6P_lg: johnson1992mgatp, sourced)

n_G6P_lg.data_reference: johnson1992mgatp; Hill coefficient of the lumped lower glycolysis in G6P, from its committed step: E. coli phosphofructokinase (PFK-1) binds fructose 6-phosphate with a Hill coefficient of 3.6 at saturating MgATP (Johnson & Reinhart 1992; "almost 4" in lebras1982proteolyzed). The lumped Hill in G6P is PFK's in F6P while phosphoglucose isomerase stays near equilibrium

K_ADP_gly.data_reference: chassagnole2002dynamic; lumped glycolysis affinity for ADP: the ADP constants of its two ATP-making steps in the E. coli kinetic model, PGK 0.185 and pyruvate kinase 0.26 mM (BIOMD0000000051)

K_Pi_gly.data_reference: eyschen1999engineered; lumped glycolysis affinity for Pi: E. coli glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase Km(Pi) 0.53 mM

K_lac.data_reference: unreferenced_placeholder; design value; no measurement found (searched 2026-10-23): lumped glycolysis product constant for lactate (no E. coli lactate dehydrogenase lactate constant). lumped glycolysis product constant for lactate

K_ATP_gly.data_reference: chassagnole2002dynamic; lumped glycolysis product constant for ATP: PGK's ATP constant 0.653 mM in the E. coli kinetic model (BIOMD0000000051)

V_hyd.data_reference: calibrated: the maintenance ATPase uses the ATP turnover that neither the H+-ATPase (25%, placeholder) nor protein turnover (protein_expression) uses

K_ATP_hyd.data_reference: unreferenced_placeholder; design value; no measurement found (searched 2026-10-23): maintenance ATPase affinity for ATP (a lumped ATPase, no single enzyme). maintenance ATPase affinity for ATP

K_ADP_hyd.data_reference: unreferenced_placeholder; design value; no measurement found (searched 2026-10-23): maintenance ATPase product constant for ADP (a lumped ATPase). maintenance ATPase product constant for ADP

K_Pi_hyd.data_reference: unreferenced_placeholder; design value; no measurement found (searched 2026-10-23): maintenance ATPase product constant for Pi (a lumped ATPase). maintenance ATPase product constant for Pi

h_lac_gly.data_reference: gnaiger1990anaerobic; glucose to lactate in bicarbonate buffer: 63 kJ released per mol lactate

h_ATP.data_reference: gajewski1986thermodynamics; enthalpy of ATP hydrolysis -20.5 kJ/mol at 25 C

C_glyc_init.data_reference: definitional; the starting cell stores nothing

store_alloc.data_reference: definitional; storage off until the player allocates energy to it

V_store_max.data_reference: derived: glycogen_store_rate x resting glycolytic flux (glycogen_store_rate: unreferenced_placeholder, placeholder; maintenance_coefficient: lynch2015bioenergetic, sourced)

K_G6P_store.data_reference: chassagnole2002dynamic; G6P affinity of the glycogen store and matrix synthesis: phosphoglucomutase, the step that takes G6P towards both, Km(G6P) 1.04 mM in the E. coli kinetic model (BIOMD0000000051, KPGMg6p)

K_ATP_store.data_reference: hill2015conserved; ATP affinity of glycogen synthesis: E. coli ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (GlgC) S0.5(ATP) 0.17 mM with its activator FBP, 2.5 mM without (Hill 2015); 1.2-1.3 mM (haugen1976biosynthesis)

C_glyc_max.data_reference: neidhardt1996chemical; glycogen ceiling: 4x the 2.5% of dry weight (about 50 mM glucose units) of balanced growth (Neidhardt & Umbarger 1996); nitrogen-limited cells given excess glucose hold more (wright1965effects)

V_mob.data_reference: derived: glycogen_mobilise_rate x resting glycolytic flux (glycogen_mobilise_rate: unreferenced_placeholder, placeholder; maintenance_coefficient: lynch2015bioenergetic, sourced)

K_glyc_mob.data_reference: chen1968purification; glycogen phosphorylase affinity for glycogen: E. coli GlgP Km 0.67% w/v (0.46% with AMP), about 41 mM glucose units

K_Pi_mob.data_reference: boeck1996purification; phosphorylase affinity for Pi: a design value, order 5 mM. The nearest measured value, E. coli maltodextrin phosphorylase (MalP) Km(Pi) 0.5 mM, would leave the phosphorylase almost saturated in Pi at rest, with no room for its rate to rise (glycogen phosphorylase itself not measured)

K_i_ATP_mob.data_reference: chen1968purification; ATP inhibits mobilisation, so glycogen is spent when ATP falls: a design stand-in for E. coli GlgP's activation by AMP (Chen & Segel 1968), which rises as ATP falls

dG0_store.data_reference: beber2022equilibrator; glucose + 2 ATP -> glycogen unit + 2 ADP + 2 Pi: 2 dG0_hyd minus the alpha-1,4 bond's hydrolysis, taken as maltose hydrolysis (-14.2 +- 3.1 kJ/mol), eQuilibrator 3.0 as dG0_hyd

h_glyc_poly.data_reference: alberty1998calculation; heat released by adding a glucose to glycogen: -0.5 kJ/mol (it absorbs 0.5 kJ), from maltose hydrolysis (Delta H -0.49 kJ/mol, Alberty's species enthalpies) for the alpha-1,4 bond

m_gly.data_reference: definitional; baseline expression of the glycolytic enzymes (the calibrated cell)

mx_alloc.data_reference: definitional; no matrix until the player allocates energy to it

V_mx_max.data_reference: derived: matrix_production_rate x resting glycolytic flux (matrix_production_rate: welman2003exopolysaccharides, placeholder; maintenance_coefficient: lynch2015bioenergetic, sourced)

K_G6P_mx.data_reference: chassagnole2002dynamic; G6P affinity of the glycogen store and matrix synthesis: phosphoglucomutase, the step that takes G6P towards both, Km(G6P) 1.04 mM in the E. coli kinetic model (BIOMD0000000051, KPGMg6p)

K_ATP_mx.data_reference: weissborn1994utp; ATP affinity of matrix synthesis: E. coli GalU (UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase, the UDP-glucose step of exopolysaccharide synthesis) Km(UTP) 0.058-0.07 mM, UTP counted as an ATP equivalent

n_ATP_mx.data_reference: derived: matrix_ATP_per_unit - 1: the first ATP phosphorylated the glucose to G6P (hexokinase, or the PTS's PEP) (matrix_ATP_per_unit: sutherland2001biofilm, placeholder)

dG0_mx.data_reference: derived: (dG0_store - 2 dG0_hyd) + matrix_ATP_per_unit x dG0_hyd - dG0_hk: the bond as in glycogen, paid by n + 1 ATP, from G6P (dG0_store: beber2022equilibrator, sourced; dG0_hyd: beber2022equilibrator, sourced; matrix_ATP_per_unit: sutherland2001biofilm, placeholder; dG0_hk: beber2022equilibrator, sourced)

h_mx_poly.data_reference: alberty1998calculation; heat released by adding a glucose unit to the matrix polymer: taken as the alpha-1,4 bond's -0.5 kJ/mol (maltose, Alberty 1998); the matrix linkages themselves are not measured
